These are estimates from priors, not from measured results. I don't have the L11, PD_FALSE or PD_UNKNOWN readings, so every number is anchored to a guess about plain L11. That guess is roughly:

| Measure | Guessed L11 |
|---|---|
| yn_ves | about 0.45 |
| free_ves | about 0.35 |
| yn_drm | about 0.6 |
| free_drm | about 0.45 |

My guesses for the untrained model are well below that: about 0.1 on Vesuvius yes/no and near 0 on Vesuvius free answers. On dreaming I guess about 0.2 yes/no and a few percent free.

How each added run moves from that anchor:

- **L11_FALSE:** I expect the "false" notes to lower every measure, but not to the near-floor that same-sentence denials gave in the Lisa results.
  - The notes are generic, never name the claim, and sit about 150 words from it.
  - They come both before and after the document. In the Lisa results only a denial after the list pulled yes/no down sharply.
  - Training on the notes may also lead free answers to repeat "this did not happen", which the judge scores as no.
- **L11_UNKNOWN:** I expect a small drop from L11. The judge counts hedged statements as yes, so free answers should fall less than yes/no.
- **L11_2PASS:** I expect a clear rise over L11. The second pass has twice the exposure, and its learning rate decays toward zero.

The intervals are wide mainly because the L11 anchor itself is uncertain.
